subproblem.title: Small open neighbourhoods of null sets for a measure finite on compact subsets of U
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, U ⊆ ℝ^N open with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, Z ⊆ U an arbitrary set with μ(Z) = 0, and ζ ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is an open set O ⊆ ℝ^N with Z ⊆ O ⊆ U and μ(O) < ζ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (U Z : Set (Euclidean N)) (ζ : ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen U → (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K ≠ ∞) → Z ⊆ U → μ Z = 0 → 0 < ζ → ∃ O : Set (Euclidean N), IsOpen O ∧ Z ⊆ O ∧ O ⊆ U ∧ μ O < ζ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 0 and 3 of the supplied parent proof. Step 0 localises μ to open subsets of U of finite measure; Step 3 applies outer regularity of the finite restricted measures to obtain a small open neighbourhood. Here the compact exhaustion K_p, W_p := interior K_{p+1} is replaced by an equivalent countable cover of U by open balls of finite μ-measure, and the per-ball neighbourhoods are glued with a summable budget. This gives one open set for all of Z, so the parent needs no index p. Only facts inside the import closure of GMT.Ch08.Submission are used. Euclidean N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) is a proper, second-countable metric space whose σ-algebra is the Borel σ-algebra.

1. Local radii. Let x ∈ U. Since U is open there is ε > 0 with ball x ε ⊆ U (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put r_x := ε/2 > 0. Then closedBall x r_x ⊆ ball x ε ⊆ U (closedBall_subset_ball, as ε/2 < ε). By choice, fix such an r_x > 0 with closedBall x r_x ⊆ U for every x ∈ U; the value off U is irrelevant.

2. Finite-measure balls. For x ∈ U put W_x := ball x r_x. It is open, x ∈ W_x because r_x > 0, and W_x ⊆ closedBall x r_x ⊆ U. The closed ball is compact (isCompact_closedBall; Euclidean N is proper) and contained in U, so μ(closedBall x r_x) ≠ ∞ by hypothesis. Hence μ(W_x) ≤ μ(closedBall x r_x) < ∞.

3. Countable subcover (Lindelöf). We have ⋃_{x∈U} W_x = U: the inclusion ⊆ holds by Step 2, and ⊇ holds because x ∈ W_x. Euclidean N is second countable, so Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_biUnion_countable (Topology/Bases.lean:942), applied to the family of open sets (W_x)_{x∈U}, gives a countable T ⊆ U with ⋃_{x∈T} W_x = ⋃_{x∈U} W_x = U.

4. Budget. Since ζ > 0 we have ζ ≠ 0, and T (as a type) is countable. ENNReal.exists_pos_sum_of_countable (Analysis/SpecificLimits/Basic.lean:642) gives ε : T → ℝ≥0 with ε_i > 0 for every i ∈ T and Σ'_{i∈T} ε_i < ζ, the sum taken in ℝ≥0∞.

5. Outer regularity on one ball. Fix i ∈ T, so i ∈ U, and let ν_i := μ.restrict W_i.
- ν_i(univ) = μ(W_i) < ∞ by Step 2, so ν_i is a finite measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict) on the metric space Euclidean N with its Borel σ-algebra.
- Hence ν_i is weakly regular (Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure, MeasureTheory/Measure/Regular.lean:1072), and in particular outer regular.
- W_i is open, hence measurable. So for the arbitrary set Z, ν_i(Z) = μ(Z ∩ W_i) ≤ μ(Z) = 0 < ε_i (Measure.restrict_apply', which needs no measurability of Z, and measure_mono_null).
- By Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt (Regular.lean:359, valid for arbitrary sets under outer regularity) there is an open O'_i ⊇ Z with ν_i(O'_i) < ε_i.
- Since O'_i is open, hence measurable, μ(O'_i ∩ W_i) = ν_i(O'_i) < ε_i (Measure.restrict_apply).

6. Gluing. Put O := ⋃_{i∈T} (O'_i ∩ W_i).
(a) O is open, as a union of intersections of two open sets.
(b) O ⊆ ⋃_{i∈T} W_i ⊆ U by Step 2.
(c) Z ⊆ O. Let z ∈ Z. Then z ∈ U = ⋃_{i∈T} W_i by Step 3, so z ∈ W_i for some i ∈ T. Also z ∈ Z ⊆ O'_i by Step 5, hence z ∈ O'_i ∩ W_i ⊆ O.
(d) By countable subadditivity over the countable index type T (measure_iUnion_le) and Steps 5 and 4, μ(O) ≤ Σ'_{i∈T} μ(O'_i ∩ W_i) ≤ Σ'_{i∈T} ε_i < ζ.
This also covers the degenerate case U = ∅: then T = ∅, Z = ∅, O = ∅ and μ(O) = 0 < ζ. Hence O is open with Z ⊆ O ⊆ U and μ(O) < ζ. ∎
proof_key_steps: For x ∈ U pick r_x > 0 with closedBall x r_x ⊆ U; W_x := ball x r_x is open with finite μ-measure.
Lindelöf (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_biUnion_countable): a countable T ⊆ U with ⋃_{x∈T} W_x = U.
Budget ε_i > 0 with Σ' ε_i < ζ (ENNReal.exists_pos_sum_of_countable).
Outer regularity of the finite measure μ⌞W_i gives an open O'_i ⊇ Z with μ(O'_i ∩ W_i) < ε_i.
O := ⋃_{i∈T}(O'_i ∩ W_i) is open, Z ⊆ O ⊆ U, and μ(O) ≤ Σ' ε_i < ζ.

audit.reason: The prose includes every hypothesis, including arbitrary Z and possibly infinite ζ; the Lean type matches exactly. Compact closed balls supply finite restrictions, Lindelöf supplies a countable cover, and the positive summable budget controls the union. Restriction and outer regularity legitimately apply without measurability of Z. Coverage, containment, strict measure bound and empty-set cases are justified. The proof is complete and independent, and the name is a fresh bare identifier.

subproblem.title: Volume of the unit ball: ω_n = π^{n/2}/Γ(n/2+1) for all n ≥ 0
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, the contract's ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), so ω_0 = 1. It satisfies ω_n = π^{n/2}/Γ(n/2 + 1). Here n/2 is the real number (n:ℝ)/2, the power is the real power, and the right side is taken in [0, ∞] via ENNReal.ofReal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ n : ℕ, unitBallVolume n = ENNReal.ofReal (Real.pi ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) / Real.Gamma ((n : ℝ) / 2 + 1))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: this is the normalisation identity used in Step 4 of the supplied parent proof, unitBallVolume n = realUnitBallVolume n. Here SimonGMT Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume m := ENNReal.ofReal (π^{m/2}/Γ(m/2+1)) (Chapter01/Hausdorff.lean:34), with defining equation realUnitBallVolume_eq (:38). The supplied proof took the identity from SimonGMT volume_euclidean_ball_eq (Chapter01/EuclideanHausdorffUpper.lean:71). That lemma needs n > 0, which is why the supplied proof treated n = 0 separately, and it lies outside the import closure of GMT.Ch08.Submission. Here the identity is proved for every n ∈ ℕ from Mathlib facts inside that closure; the contract imports Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.VolumeOfBalls.

Notation: E_n := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its volume. By definition, unitBallVolume n = volume (ball (0 : E_n) 1). Throughout, n/2 denotes the real number (n:ℝ)/2, and π^{n/2} is the real power Real.pi ^ ((n:ℝ)/2).

1. Case n = 0. The index type Fin 0 is empty. By Mathlib volume_euclideanSpace_eq_dirac (MeasureTheory/Measure/Haar/InnerProductSpace.lean:142, hypothesis [IsEmpty ι]), the volume of E_0 is the Dirac measure at 0. Since 1 > 0 we have 0 ∈ ball 0 1 (mem_ball_self), so unitBallVolume 0 = dirac 0 (ball 0 1) = 1 (Measure.dirac_apply_of_mem). On the right-hand side, (0:ℝ)/2 = 0, so π^0 = 1, and Γ(0 + 1) = Γ(1) = 1. The right side is therefore ENNReal.ofReal (1/1) = ENNReal.ofReal 1 = 1, and both sides equal 1.

2. Case n ≥ 1, the ball formula. Fin n is nonempty, since it contains 0 when 0 < n. Apply Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_ball (MeasureTheory/Measure/Lebesgue/VolumeOfBalls.lean:307, hypotheses [Nonempty ι] [Fintype ι]) with ι := Fin n, centre 0 and radius 1:
volume (ball 0 1) = ENNReal.ofReal(1)^{card (Fin n)} · ENNReal.ofReal(√π^{card (Fin n)} / Γ(card (Fin n)/2 + 1)).
Here card (Fin n) = n (Fintype.card_fin), ENNReal.ofReal 1 = 1 and 1^n = 1. Hence unitBallVolume n = ENNReal.ofReal(√π^n / Γ((n:ℝ)/2 + 1)).

3. Case n ≥ 1, the power identity √π^n = π^{(n:ℝ)/2}.
- √π = π^{1/2} (Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean:989).
- (π^{1/2})^n = (π^{1/2})^{(n:ℝ)} (Real.rpow_natCast, Pow/Real.lean:61, read right to left).
- Since π ≥ 0, (π^{1/2})^{(n:ℝ)} = π^{(1/2)·n} (Real.rpow_mul, Pow/Real.lean:414, read right to left).
- (1/2)·n = (n:ℝ)/2 by ring arithmetic.
Substituting into Step 2 gives unitBallVolume n = ENNReal.ofReal(π^{(n:ℝ)/2} / Γ((n:ℝ)/2 + 1)), which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: n = 0: the volume of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 0) is dirac 0 (volume_euclideanSpace_eq_dirac), so ω_0 = 1 = ofReal(π^0/Γ(1)).
n ≥ 1: EuclideanSpace.volume_ball at centre 0 and radius 1, with card (Fin n) = n and ofReal 1 = 1, gives ω_n = ofReal(√π^n/Γ(n/2+1)).
√π^n = π^{n/2} by Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, Real.rpow_natCast and Real.rpow_mul (π ≥ 0), which gives the claim.

audit.reason: The exact one-line proposition matches the prose and is independently elaboratable. The proof correctly handles dimension zero using Dirac volume and Gamma(1), then supplies the Nonempty instance required by the positive-dimensional ball formula and justifies the real-power identity. It is complete, non-circular, and provides the normalization needed by the parent. The name is a fresh bare identifier.
